name: Porphyritic-Inselberg
description: Dust finer than flour pools in the low places, swallowing craters to their rims. Nothing has disturbed solar wind erosion patterns in a million years, and the dust keeps its surface smooth as held breath.
The air carries wet iron and lichen, and sound behaves strangely: footsteps crack loud, then die without echo. At night the temperature drops fast enough to hear the rock tick as it contracts.
Local legend among spacers says the planet hums on a frequency just below hearing. Instruments confirm it. Nobody agrees on the source.
Survey contracts pay double for reasons nobody writes down. Veterans read the fine print, then read the survivors.
